Let me analyze the conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi"
- Document: "Esit Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi"

Differences:
- "ESIT" vs "Esit" — case difference
- "Imalat" vs "İmalat" — Turkish dotted capital İ vs I (accent difference)
- "Sirketi" vs "Şirketi" — Turkish Ş vs S (accent difference)
- "Limited Sirketi" vs "Limited Şirketi" — same, accent difference

These are clearly the same company: accent differences and case differences = same-entity. The document value carries proper Turkish diacritics (İ, Ş), which is more accurate for a Turkish company name. The rule says: accent differences = same-entity. Best value — the rules don't explicitly say which form to use for same-entity for applicant. For certificate numbers, "number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." For spelling/accent drift, it doesn't specify best_value, but the natural choice is the document's value since the certificate is the legal instrument and it has the correct diacritics. Actually the rule for different-entity says best_value = document's because certificate is legal instrument. For same-entity spelling drift, presumably either; but the richer, correctly accented form from the document is better. I'll pick the document's value.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value = "Esit Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi".
